title: A tensor section has affine nonvanishing locus when one factor does
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_n$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $t_i$ be global sections of $\mathcal L_i$. Write $\tau=t_1\otimes\cdots\otimes t_n$ for the induced global section of the tensor product $\mathcal L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\cdots\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and let $X_{t_i}$ and $X_\tau$ be their nonvanishing loci [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X_\tau=\bigcap_i X_{t_i}$. If one $X_{t_i}$ is affine, then $X_\tau$ is affine.

proof.text: For two factors apply the tensor-fibre isomorphism and section-value formula of lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor, with f the identity. An isomorphism preserves nonzero values. Over a field, singleton families consisting of nonzero vectors are linearly independent; Mathlib LinearIndependent.tmul_of_flat_left makes their tensor family linearly independent, hence its single tensor nonzero. Conversely a zero factor gives a zero tensor. Thus the two-factor locus is the intersection. This does not need rank-one bases.

proof.text: Given an affine factor locus U=X_{t_j}, use Finset.induction_on to intersect U with any finite set of factor loci. The empty set leaves U; insertion applies the first clause of lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open to the previously obtained affine open and the inserted factor section. Apply this to Finset.univ. The extra U condition is redundant since every point in all factor loci is in X_{t_j}=U. Combine with the previously proved tensor-locus equality.
